exposure: Characteristics of paediatric cardiac fitness programmes (duration, session frequency, eligible patient populations, mode of delivery, equipment, incentives, funding sources, cost)
Status of programme enrollment and development
outcome: Landscape of paediatric cardiac fitness programmes
Variability in programme structure and implementation
Perceived effectiveness of programmes in improving quality of life/wellness, cardiovascular fitness, and neuromuscular strength
cohort: The cohort consisted of 40 individuals from 23 centres in 6 countries (predominantly US-based) who are members of the Global Coalition for Fitness and Congenital Heart Disease (GloCo) and provide exercise-based interventions for children and young adults with congenital and acquired heart disease.
finding: Paediatric cardiac fitness programmes are a growing international field with diverse applications, but significant variability in their structure and implementation creates barriers to developing consensus guidelines and achieving standardised care.
cross-section timing: At the time of the survey distribution and completion (current landscape)
